boundary: Source identifiers and agent derivations are research evidence only. Original copyright, seven-component custody, official key, independent academic review and owner approval all remain outstanding.

source_discrepancy.printed_finding: Original pie chart supplies Mathematics 35% and English 15%; with Maths count 140, English count is 60.
source_discrepancy.owner_compilation_claim: Owner supplies a textual reconstruction of the pie-chart sectors, not the original chart figure.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Use the given Mathematics sector's 35% and known absolute count to recover the full population, then apply a different 15% English sector to that same total.
protected_capability_research.math_warrant: Maths 35%=140 gives total 140/(35/100)=400 students; English 15% of 400=60. The two percentages refer to the same complete pie-chart population.
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Multiply English share by 140, confuse a sector percentage with a count, or treat the owner text-only chart reconstruction as original-figure custody.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: Requires the intact source pie-chart sectors, a common total and confirmed percent labels; the pie chart is not retained or licensed. Conflict 004 is a chart-dependency/source-figure custody issue.

source_math_research.previous_agent_math_explanation: Pie-chart sectors sum to 360; Hindi 70deg + Social Science 55deg =125deg. Total 720 => 125*(720/360)=250 marks.

source_discrepancy.printed_finding: Printed consecutive original Q32 and Q33 share one pie chart and are distinct question positions.
source_discrepancy.owner_compilation_claim: Owner groups both as one compilation entry Q38 with subparts i and ii.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Recognize two requested school subjects as distinct angle sectors of one 360° pie; sum their sector angles, then convert that combined angle into marks out of the printed total.
protected_capability_research.math_warrant: Hindi 70° plus Social Science 55°=125°; 720 total marks ÷360°=2 marks/degree, giving 250 marks for the pair.
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Use percentages as if the numbers 70 and 55 were marks, or count only one of the two indicated sectors.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: The two printed sectors and their labels must come from the authentic shared chart; source printed Q32 is independent from Q33 even though owner compilation merges them. Conflict 008.

source_discrepancy.printed_finding: Printed consecutive original Q32 and Q33 share one pie chart and are distinct question positions.
source_discrepancy.owner_compilation_claim: Owner groups both as one compilation entry Q38 with subparts i and ii.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Compute the missing Mathematics sector as the remainder of a full 360° pie after the four labelled sector angles, then convert that angular share to percentage.
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Divide residual angle by 100 instead of 360, or collapse separately printed Q33 into owner Q38 subpart ii as if it were one original question.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: Shares the source figure and conflict 008 with printed Q32, but has a distinct protected complement-to-percentage inference and separate printed source ID.

source_math_research.previous_agent_math_explanation: P: midpoint 10 and upper limit 15 give lower limit 2×10−15=5, Column II (ii). Q: range of listed values is max93−min18=75, (iii). R: 0.4 cm/50 people for 2500 people is 0.4×50=20 cm, (i). Printed option C.
source_math_research.previous_agent_check: For P, (5+15)/2=10; for R, 20cm divided by 0.4cm per 50 people gives 50×50=2500 people, and the extremal values 93 and 18 occur in the list.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Audit each match independently: invert class mark for missing class boundary, compute range from actual maximum/minimum, and scale the graph length through a stated length-per-people rate.
protected_capability_research.math_warrant: P: midpoint 10 and upper endpoint 15 imply lower endpoint 5. Q: range 93−18=75. R: graph scale 0.4 cm/50 people gives (2500/50)×0.4=20 cm; source pairing P-ii, Q-iii, R-i.
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Confuse class-mark midpoint with interval width, subtract arbitrary data points for range, or multiply 0.4 by 2500 without normalization to 50 people.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: Three distinct statistics statements are juxtaposed in one matching source position; require original column labels and complete choice order before any Core2 representation.

source_math_research.previous_agent_math_explanation: Of 400 surveyed, 250 work in government offices, leaving 150 in the private sector. Under equally likely selection from the survey, P(private)=150/400=3/8, printed choice B.
source_math_research.previous_agent_check: Private probability 3/8 plus government 5/8 is 1; integer count 400×3/8=150.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Establish that government and private-sector respondents are exhaustive mutually exclusive outcomes of one uniform sample; subtract known government count from full sample before forming probability.
protected_capability_research.math_warrant: 400 surveyed, government 250, private 400−250=150; selecting uniformly from 400 gives 150/400=3/8. Complement P(private)+P(government)=1.
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Use 250/400 for the requested private event, or divide by the government subgroup rather than all surveyed people.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: Probability uses an equally likely individual from a complete two-class surveyed population; do not infer it applies to other unlisted employment categories.

source_math_research.previous_agent_math_explanation: A bag containing three red, five black and four white balls has twelve equally likely choices. The five favourable black balls yield probability 5/12, printed option C.
source_math_research.previous_agent_check: P(red)+P(black)+P(white)=3/12+5/12+4/12=1, verifying the sample-space partition. The favourable count is strictly between zero and the full set of 12 outcomes.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Treat all individual balls as equally likely elementary outcomes; count favorable black balls versus the full bag, not the number of distinct colours.
protected_capability_research.math_warrant: Three red + five black + four white balls =12 equally likely draws; black outcomes=5, so P(black)=5/12. All colours partition 12/12.
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Use 1/3 because there are three colours or use 5/(3+4) excluding the favorable balls.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: One draw from equally likely balls, not repeated independent draws or uniform probability over colour labels.

source_math_research.previous_agent_math_explanation: Two independent six-sided dice have 36 equiprobable ordered outcomes. Sums greater than nine are 10 (3 ways), 11 (2 ways), 12 (1 way): 6 favorable outcomes, giving 6/36=1/6, option C.
source_math_research.previous_agent_check: Explicit ordered pairs: (4,6),(5,5),(6,4),(5,6),(6,5),(6,6), six outcomes out of 36.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Model the two independent fair dice as 6×6=36 equally likely ordered pairs and count precisely those whose total is greater than nine.
protected_capability_research.math_warrant: Sum 10 occurs in 3 ordered pairs, 11 in 2, and 12 in 1; 6 of 36 gives 1/6. Pairs: (4,6),(5,5),(6,4),(5,6),(6,5),(6,6).
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Treat (4,6) and (6,4) as one equiprobable outcome, or count sums 9 or more rather than strictly greater than nine.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: Requires two independently and fairly rolled labelled dice; distinguish ordered elementary outcomes from unordered numeric sums.

source_math_research.previous_agent_math_explanation: There are 50 distinct integers from 51 through 100 inclusive. Exactly ten are prime (53,59,61,67,71,73,79,83,89,97); the other 40 are not prime. Thus probability =40/50=4/5, printed D.
source_math_research.previous_agent_check: The ten primes are all >50 and <=100, so the complement is 1−10/50=40/50; prime and nonprime probabilities sum to one.

protected_capability_research.decisive_inference: Count the inclusive 51–100 card interval first, enumerate the prime-labelled subset accurately, then take its nonprime complement.
protected_capability_research.math_warrant: The 50 distinct integers 51 to 100 contain ten primes 53,59,61,67,71,73,79,83,89,97; 40 nonprime cards out of 50 yield 4/5. Complement primes 1/5.
protected_capability_research.plausible_wrong_path_unobserved: Count endpoints exclusively (49 instead of 50), assume even numbers only are composite or treat every odd number as prime.
protected_capability_research.conditions_and_limits: Each card in the consecutive inclusive interval is equally likely; nonprime includes composites, while the outside-interval status of 1 is irrelevant.
